original.reason: The additive-subgroup conclusion uses the difference criterion without first establishing nonemptiness, and the multiplication argument introduces an unbound variable x after quantifying r and b. These are repairable proof gaps, but the presented proof is not fully rigorous.

judgment.reason: It establishes nonemptiness, closure under subtraction, and absorption under multiplication by arbitrary ring elements. In a commutative ring this proves the ideal condition.
It correctly verifies the additive subgroup criterion and closure under multiplication by arbitrary ring elements.
It correctly proves additive-subgroup closure and multiplicative absorption, sufficient for an ideal in a commutative ring.
It correctly verifies all required ideal properties.
